SPIREBROTHERS-ROAD_TRIP_TO_GRANDMAS.page:
Somehow the whole Idaho crew fits in Tim's minivan. Mostly. Somebody is sitting on a cooler.

Grandma lives way down south, past Daniel's place, and Dad has already announced that [gold]this van makes good time[/gold].

[blue]How do you want to do the drive?[/blue]
Stop at Every Rest Area
Dad's rule. Heal [blue]20%[/blue] of your Max HP.
Drive Straight Through
Lose [red]5[/red] HP. Gain [blue]50[/blue] [gold]Gold[/gold]. You saved on the motel.
Swing by Daniel's
Daniel tunes up the van. [gold]Upgrade[/gold] [blue]2[/blue] random cards.

Every rest area. Every single one. Dad stretches at each of them like he's about to run a marathon.

It takes forever, but everyone shows up rested and in a surprisingly good mood.

Grandma is already waiting on the porch.

Gas station snacks for dinner. Somebody's elbow in your ribs the whole way. David keeps a running total of the money you're saving.

You roll up at sunrise, stiff and a little proud of yourselves.

Grandma is already waiting on the porch.

Daniel meets you in the driveway with a toolbox and a look. [gold]"When was the last time anyone checked the oil?"[/gold]

An hour later the van runs better than it has in years, and you have heard a lot about spark plugs.

Grandma is already waiting on the porch.
Choose a story to remember
Grandma's Cooking
Gain [blue]6[/blue] Max HP.
Grandma Slips You Some Cash
"Don't tell your mother." Gain [blue]75[/blue] [gold]Gold[/gold].
Listen to Grandma's Stories
Choose [blue]1[/blue] of [blue]3[/blue] cards to add to your [gold]Deck[/gold]. They're already [gold]Upgraded[/gold].

Nobody leaves Grandma's table hungry. Nobody is allowed to.

You waddle back to the van with a plate of leftovers wrapped in foil.

She presses a folded bill into your hand on the way out, like it's a secret mission.

You are a grown adult. You take it anyway.

She tells the one about when Dad was a kid. Then the one before that. Then a new one nobody has ever heard.

You're going to remember this one.
SPIREBROTHERS-THANKSGIVING_WITH_MOM_AND_:
The whole family is home. Mom has been cooking since before sunrise, Dad is out back with the turkey fryer, and there are more kids running through the kitchen than anyone can count.

[blue]There's a lot going on. Where do you want to be?[/blue]
Heal [blue]30%[/blue] of your Max HP. Add a [red]Food Coma[/red] to your [gold]Deck[/gold].

Dad lowers the bird into the fryer with the focus of a man defusing a bomb. Everyone else watches from a very safe distance.

It comes out golden and perfect. It always does. Nobody knows how.

Mom made every single thing on this table, and the pie might be the best of it.

One more slice can't hurt. It can, actually. You will be on this couch for the rest of the day.

Mom always does the dishes, and she always says she doesn't need help. You grab a towel anyway.

She washes, you dry, and you get caught up on everything. The kitchen has never been cleaner.

The boys drift out to Dad's shop, like they always do. He has a project going, and it needs "just a couple more hands."

Three hours later it's finished, and you know your way around a few tools you'd never touched before.

Nobody spends Thanksgiving alone if the boys' mom hears about it, so you got the invite years ago. Now you're just on the list.

She has been cooking since before sunrise, their dad is out back with the turkey fryer, and there are more kids running through the kitchen than anyone can count.

[blue]There's a lot going on. Where do you want to be?[/blue]
Heal [blue]30%[/blue] of your Max HP. Add a [red]Food Coma[/red] to your [gold]Deck[/gold].

The boys' dad lowers the bird into the fryer with the focus of a man defusing a bomb. Everyone else watches from a very safe distance.

It comes out golden and perfect. It always does. Nobody knows how.

Their mom made every single thing on this table, and she keeps putting more of it on your plate.

One more slice can't hurt. It can, actually. You will be on this couch for the rest of the day.

Their mom always does the dishes, and she always says guests don't help. You grab a towel anyway.

She washes, you dry, and she wants to hear everything you've been up to. The kitchen has never been cleaner.

You drift out to the shop with the boys, like everybody does. Their dad has a project going, and it needs "just a couple more hands."

Three hours later it's finished, and you know your way around a few tools you'd never touched before.
SPIREBROTHERS-DAY_AT_THE_LAKE.title: A Day at the Lake
SPIREBROTHERS-DAY_AT_THE_LAKE.pages.INIT:
Mom and Dad have been out on the lake since dawn. The boat is gassed up, the poles are rigged, and Mom is already in the water.

[blue]Sun's out. What's the plan?[/blue]
See what bites. Maybe a [gold]potion[/gold], maybe [gold]Gold[/gold], maybe a [gold]relic[/gold]. Maybe a boot.
Lose [red]8[/red] HP. Gain [blue]5[/blue] Max HP. Worth it.
SPIREBROTHERS-DAY_AT_THE_LAKE.pages.CAUG:
Something tugs on the line. Dad grabs the net.

It's not a fish. It's a [gold]little glass bottle[/gold], cork still in. Dad says that counts.

No bites all morning. Then, right before lunch, your hook snags a [gold]coin purse[/gold] somebody dropped off the dock years ago.

Dad insists you were reeling it in wrong.

The line goes tight and stays tight. It takes both of you to haul it up.

It's... honestly, you're not sure what it is. But it's [gold]definitely[/gold] yours now.

You catch a boot.

Dad takes a picture of you holding it. He'll be showing that picture to people for years.
SPIREBROTHERS-DAY_AT_THE_LAKE.pages.WAKE:
You stay up for about four seconds, and then the lake hits you like a wall.

Mom gives you a 10 for effort. You go again. And again.
SPIREBROTHERS-DAY_AT_THE_LAKE.pages.LOUN:
Warm boards, cold drink, feet in the water.

Somewhere out on the lake, Dad is yelling that he got one. You'll believe it when you see it.
SPIREBROTHERS-DAY_AT_THE_LAKE.pages.FRIE:
The boys' parents have been out on the lake since dawn. The boat is gassed up, the poles are rigged, and their mom is already in the water, waving you in.

[blue]Sun's out. What's the plan?[/blue]
See what bites. Maybe a [gold]potion[/gold], maybe [gold]Gold[/gold], maybe a [gold]relic[/gold]. Maybe a boot.
Lose [red]8[/red] HP. Gain [blue]5[/blue] Max HP. Worth it.

Something tugs on the line. The boys' dad grabs the net.

It's not a fish. It's a [gold]little glass bottle[/gold], cork still in. He says that counts.

No bites all morning. Then, right before lunch, your hook snags a [gold]coin purse[/gold] somebody dropped off the dock years ago.

The boys' dad insists you were reeling it in wrong.

The line goes tight and stays tight. It takes you and the boys' dad both to haul it up.

It's... honestly, you're not sure what it is. But it's [gold]definitely[/gold] yours now.

You catch a boot.

The boys' dad takes a picture of you holding it. It goes in the family album. You're in the family album now.

You stay up for about four seconds, and then the lake hits you like a wall.

The boys' mom gives you a 10 for effort. You go again. And again.

Warm boards, cold drink, feet in the water.

Somewhere out on the lake, the boys' dad is yelling that he got one. You'll believe it when you see it.
SPIREBROTHERS-FAMILY_HIKE.title: Family Hike
Boots laced, water bottles filled. The trailhead sign lists three routes, and Dad is already reading the one at the top out loud.

[blue]Which way is the family going?[/blue]
Heal [blue]15%[/blue] of your Max HP. Gain [blue]4[/blue] Max HP.
Heal [blue]10%[/blue] of your Max HP. Get a random [gold]potion[/gold].
SPIREBROTHERS-FAMILY_HIKE.pages.GO_FOR_T:
Your legs are on fire for the last mile. Dad is somehow not even breathing hard.

But the view from the top makes everything feel small and simple for a minute.
SPIREBROTHERS-FAMILY_HIKE.pages.TAKE_THE:
Wildflowers, a creek, a lot of stopping to look at things.

Nobody is in a hurry. That's the whole point.
SPIREBROTHERS-FAMILY_HIKE.pages.TURN_BAC:
About half a mile in, someone mentions the ice cream place by the trailhead.

The vote is unanimous. Nobody regrets it.
SPIREBROTHERS-CALLING_MOM.title: Calling Mom
There's a quiet moment between fights, and you find yourself dialing without really deciding to.

She picks up on the second ring, like always. [gold]"Hi, honey! What's going on?"[/gold]
Daniel doesn't vent. He just fixes it.
SPIREBROTHERS-CALLING_MOM.pages.JUST_CHA:
You talk about nothing in particular for twenty minutes. The weather. The dog. What Dad caught last weekend.

You feel better than you have in days.
SPIREBROTHERS-CALLING_MOM.pages.ASK_FOR_:
She listens to the whole thing, then asks one question that makes you look at it completely differently.

She's annoyingly good at that.
SPIREBROTHERS-CALLING_MOM.pages.VENT_FOR:
You talk. And talk. She says "mm-hm" at all the right moments.

By the end, you can't even remember why half of it bothered you. [gold]"Love you, honey. Call me Sunday."[/gold]
SPIREBROTHERS-CALLING_MOM.pages.FRIEND_I:
Your phone buzzes. It's the boys' mom. She got your number years ago "for emergencies," and she has never once used it for an emergency.

[gold]"Hi, honey! The boys say you're all climbing some tower. Are you eating?"[/gold]
SPIREBROTHERS-CALLING_MOM.pages.FRIEND_J:
Twenty minutes about nothing in particular. The weather. Her garden. What the boys' dad caught last weekend, and whether you've been sleeping.

She tells you to come for dinner sometime. She means it.
SPIREBROTHERS-CALLING_MOM.pages.FRIEND_A:
You weren't going to ask her anything. Somehow you tell her the whole thing anyway.

One question from her, and it looks completely different. Now you know where the boys get it.
SPIREBROTHERS-CALLING_MOM.pages.FRIEND_V:
You talk. And talk. She says "mm-hm" at all the right moments, like you're one of her own.

By the end, you can't even remember why half of it bothered you. [gold]"Love you, honey. Tell the boys to call me."[/gold]
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.title: Insult Duel
A pirate steps out of the shadows. His beard is perfectly, impossibly square. A parrot on his shoulder squawks his name for him: [gold]"Captain Blockbeard!"[/gold]

"I challenge you to a duel! Not of swords. Of [gold]wits[/gold]. Best two out of three. If you lose, you pay."

[blue]He looks very confident.[/blue]
He insults, you answer. Win [blue]2[/blue] rounds to take a [gold]relic[/gold]. Lose [blue]2[/blue] and you pay up, or fight him.
Nothing happens. He will remember this.
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pages.WALK_AWA:
"Coward!" he shouts after you. "I'll tell everyone! Every port! Every tavern!"

The parrot repeats it a few more times, just to be sure you heard.
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pages.ROUND.de:
{Result}Blockbeard puffs up his chest:
[gold]"{Insult}"[/gold]

[blue]Your answers: {Wins}    His: {Losses}[/blue]
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pages.TOUCHE.d: [green]Touché![/green] He opens his mouth, closes it, and turns a little red. The parrot snickers.
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pages.MISS.des: [red]That... doesn't really answer it.[/red] He roars with laughter. The parrot laughs too, which somehow hurts more.
[green]Touché![/green] Blockbeard stands there with his mouth open, but nothing comes out.

Finally he digs through his coat and shoves something into your hands. "Take it! Just... take it, and don't tell anyone."
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pages.DEFEAT.d:
[red]Two misses.[/red] Blockbeard slaps his knee and wipes a tear from his eye.

"That settles it! Now, about my payment..."
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pages.PAY_UP.d:
He counts every coin twice, bites one of them, and tips his hat.

"A pleasure doing business! Come back when you've practiced!"
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.0.insult: My cutlass has seen more battles than you've had hot dinners!
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.0.comeba: Judging by the rust, it lost most of them.
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.1.insult: I've built better crews out of dirt blocks!
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.1.comeba: That explains the smell on your ship.
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.2.insult: You swing that thing like you're swatting flies!
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.2.comeba: Only because they keep following you around.
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.3.insult: Nobody has ever beaten me in a duel!
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.3.comeba: Nobody has ever wanted to stand that close to you.
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.4.insult: I'll have you swabbing my decks by sundown!
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.4.comeba: Your decks haven't seen a mop since your beard was a mustache.
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.5.insult: Every port on the sea knows my name!
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.5.comeba: Sure, from the wanted posters. They really captured your good side.
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.6.insult: My parrot is smarter than the lot of you!
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.6.comeba: Is that why it does all the talking?
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.7.insult: This beard is square for a reason!
SPIREBROTHERS-INSULT_DUEL.pairs.7.comeba: Yes, somebody tried to build a house in it.
SPIREBROTHERS-ROAD_TRIP_TO_GRANDMAS.page: Let Huffman Pick the Route
His route is the driveway. Heal [blue]30%[/blue] of your Max HP. Gain [blue]3[/blue] Max HP.

Huffman makes it to the end of the block before he starts listing everything that could go wrong on a twelve-hour drive. Gas station bathrooms come up. Several times.

By the second stoplight, the van is pointed back at his house. [gold]"I'll make chicken. Everybody likes chicken."[/gold]

Everybody does like chicken. Grandma gets a long phone call instead, and nobody has to sit on the cooler.
SPIREBROTHERS-WEEKEND_IN_TOWN.title: Weekend in Town
SPIREBROTHERS-WEEKEND_IN_TOWN.pages.INIT:
David is in town for the weekend, staying with John and Huffman.

John picked him up at the airport. Huffman said he'd [gold]"see him at the house,"[/gold] and he meant it.

[blue]How should the weekend go?[/blue]
He's not going out. He's frying. Gain [blue]7[/blue] Max HP.
He has a spreadsheet and coupons. Gain [blue]60[/blue] [gold]Gold[/gold].
SPIREBROTHERS-WEEKEND_IN_TOWN.pages.RAID:
"One more pull" turns into eleven more pulls. John has a spreadsheet of cooldowns open on his second monitor, and David keeps suggesting a better one.

The sun is coming up when the boss finally drops. Everyone is exhausted. Everyone got better at this.
SPIREBROTHERS-WEEKEND_IN_TOWN.pages.DINN:
Huffman has a deep fryer and no fear. Chicken. Fries. Pickles. Something that might have been a vegetable once.

The Mastiff gets a plate too. Nobody leaves the couch for the rest of the night, and Huffman considers it the best weekend he's had all year.
SPIREBROTHERS-WEEKEND_IN_TOWN.pages.LET_:
David has the whole weekend mapped out: free museum day, a two-for-one lunch, and a gas station with the cheapest fuel in the county.

John and Huffman complain the entire time. At the end, David reads out how much everyone saved, and they have to admit it's a lot.
SPIREBROTHERS-DAY_AT_HOME.title: A Day at Home
A quiet afternoon at Brandi's.

The bathroom door is shut, for the toilet paper's sake. There's gray fur on every cushion. Lily Bean is spinning in circles by the leash hook, and Yertle is watching from her tank. Judging.

[blue]Who gets your afternoon?[/blue]
Beep boop. Add [gold]Peppi[/gold] to your deck.
Feed her. Lose [red]8[/red] HP. Obtain a random [gold]Relic[/gold].
SPIREBROTHERS-DAY_AT_HOME.pages.PLAY_WIT:
Peppi can't really meow. She looks right at you and goes [gold]"beep boop."[/gold]

Someone left the bathroom door open a crack. By the time you find her, the toilet paper is confetti, and she looks extremely proud of herself.
SPIREBROTHERS-DAY_AT_HOME.pages.BRUSH_FE:
Felicity purrs through the whole brushing. When you're done, there's a second, smaller gray cat's worth of fur on the floor.

You're covered in it. It's warm, at least.
SPIREBROTHERS-DAY_AT_HOME.pages.WALK_LIL:
Lily Bean pulls her pink leash the whole way around the block, stops to sniff every single mailbox, and snorts at a leaf.

You come back tired and happy. So does she. She falls asleep on your foot.
SPIREBROTHERS-DAY_AT_HOME.pages.FEED_YER:
Yertle is twenty-two years old. She had three brothers once. She ate them.

She takes the food. She also takes a chunk of your finger. While you're looking for a bandage, you notice something shiny at the bottom of her tank.
